record.paper_title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let B = {B(s,t)}_{s,t≥0} be a two-parameter Brownian sheet in R^d, meaning a centered Gaussian process with covariance Cov(B_i(s,t), B_j(u,v)) = min(s,u) min(t,v) δ_{i,j}. For d ∈ {2,3}, fix any slice parameter s > 0 and consider the zero set of the slice, equivalently B^{-1}{0} ∩ ({s} × (0,∞)). Is it true that, outside one null event that works simultaneously for every s > 0, this set is finite for every s > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B=\{B(s,t)\}_{s,t\ge 0}$ be a two-parameter Brownian sheet taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$; that is, $B$ is a centered Gaussian process with independent components and covariance
$$\operatorname{Cov}(B_i(s,t), B_j(u,v)) = \min(s,u)\,\min(t,v)\,\delta_{i,j}, \qquad 1\le i,j\le d.$$
For each fixed $s>0$, consider the zero set of the corresponding slice:
$$Z_s := B^{-1}\{0\} \cap (\{s\}\times(0,\infty)) = \{(s,t): t>0,\ B(s,t)=0\}.$$
Assume $d\in\{2,3\}$. Prove or disprove: there exists a single $\mathbb{P}$-null event $N$ such that, on the complement of $N$, the set $Z_s$ is finite for every $s>0$ simultaneously.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for recent work on zeros of the Brownian sheet (including Khoshnevisan's open problems list and the 2024 preprint "Zeros of the Brownian Sheet", arXiv:2405.20019) indicates that recent results address Khoshnevisan's Open Problem 4 concerning Hausdorff dimension of projections of the zero set, but do not resolve the question of simultaneous finiteness of slice zero sets for all s>0 in dimensions d=2,3. No source found that proves or disproves this statement, so it appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Zeros of the Brownian Sheet
status_evidence.snippet: The authors study zeros of the Brownian sheet and resolve a question of Khoshnevisan concerning projections of the zero set affecting Hausdorff dimension, but do not address simultaneous finiteness of slice zero sets in d=2,3.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on zeros of the Brownian sheet concerns a different open problem (projections/Hausdorff dimension), not the simultaneous-finiteness question.

status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 1. Suppose d in {2,3}. Is it true that outside a single null set, B^{-1}{0} cap ({s} x (0,infty)) is a finite set for all s>0?
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem by Khoshnevisan.
